what:
speed-sol-core (lane core's speed of light): one load for what blaze-mem has committed.

Where: crates/blaze-mem/src/tag.rs, and the one caller crates/blaze-graph/src/arena.rs `own()` (lane core's; speed-sol-core asks you to make that one-line edit too, so both land together).

Why: `blaze_graph::arena::own()` is `held() + blaze_mem::tag::snapshot().committed`. `snapshot()` folds the thread's pending counts and reads 5 counters of each of the 20 tags (100 relaxed loads over 20 cache lines that every worker keeps writing with `fetch_add`), to use one field, `COMMITTED.now`. On the owner thread of `exec::Scheduler` that is about 20 contended misses, roughly 2 us, each time the plane hears what blaze holds (now once per batch of up to 64 messages, with a budget only; it was after every Done). One load is about 5 ns.

Exact edit:
1. crates/blaze-mem/src/tag.rs, after `pub fn headroom`:
    /// Bytes committed in every region now: [`Snapshot::committed`] without the rest of a
    /// snapshot, one load.
    pub fn committed_now() -> u64 {
        COMMITTED.now.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
2. crates/blaze-graph/src/arena.rs `own()`:
    held().saturating_add(blaze_mem::tag::committed_now())
   and its doc's `[blaze_mem::tag::Snapshot::committed]` link becomes `[blaze_mem::tag::committed_now]`.
Same value as before (the field snapshot reads), so no test changes; `snapshot()` stays for its other callers.

history.note: crates/blaze-mem/src/tag.rs: `pub fn committed_now() -> u64` added after `headroom` as asked (one relaxed load of COMMITTED.now). The blaze-graph/src/arena.rs own() edit is lane core's path, filed to core as 00890 with the exact edit.
